_what_this_is: Tier-G Ingredient KB entry for snail secretion filtrate (snail mucin) — ADR-002 quality bar. Agent-adversarially reviewed; every claim carries a mechanism and a verified, resolvable citation. Mirrors ingredient_kb.genistein_soy_isoflavones.json in shape.

ingredient.what_it_is: A filtered, purified secretion from land snails (primarily Helix aspersa / Cornu aspersum). Contains a mixture of glycoproteins, glycosaminoglycans (including hyaluronic acid), allantoin, glycolic acid, copper peptides, and polyphenols. Works primarily as a humectant; allantoin contributes a soothing appearance; low-concentration glycolic acid provides mild surface-renewal action.

marketing_vs_reality.reality: The dominant cosmetic actions are humectancy (glycosaminoglycans/HA draw and hold moisture) and soothing appearance (allantoin). Clinical evidence of actual tissue repair in intact human skin is limited to small, mostly uncontrolled studies. The wound-healing data comes primarily from animal models and minor wounds — it cannot be extrapolated to cosmetic skin 'repair'. Cosmetic-appropriate language: 'helps skin look and feel smoother and more comfortable.'

Animal wound-healing studies show upregulated COL3A1 expression, but these are full-thickness excisional wound models in mice — not intact cosmetic skin. No peer-reviewed RCT in healthy human skin demonstrates measurable collagen synthesis increase from SSF alone.

overview: Snail secretion filtrate is primarily a humectant-plus-soothing agent. Its blend of hyaluronic acid–class glycosaminoglycans and glycoproteins helps skin retain moisture and look plumper; allantoin lends a calming, smoothing appearance; trace glycolic acid contributes mild surface-cell renewal. Controlled clinical evidence is modest (small-N trials, single-center), but hydration and comfort improvements are the most consistently replicated findings. 'Regeneration' framing exceeds what the cosmetic evidence supports.

benefits.what_it_means: Skin feels more comfortable and looks plumper with regular use. One double-blind RCT (n=50) showed significantly reduced transepidermal water loss vs. vehicle after 12 weeks.
benefits.mechanism: Glycosaminoglycans (including hyaluronic acid) in SSF attract and bind water molecules in the stratum corneum (humectant action), reducing TEWL.

benefits.what_it_means: Skin looks calmer and feels less rough after use. Allantoin is the primary driver; it has a long record in cosmetic and wound-care formulations for smoothing appearance.
benefits.mechanism: Allantoin promotes desquamation of corneocytes and has keratolytic-soothing properties at cosmetic concentrations, reducing the appearance of roughness and irritation.

benefits.what_it_means: Minor contribution to smoother skin texture over time. Effect is subtle at the concentrations naturally present in formulations — not equivalent to a dedicated AHA treatment.
benefits.mechanism: Glycolic acid (an alpha-hydroxy acid) loosens corneocyte adhesion at the skin surface, accelerating cell turnover. Concentrations in SSF are low, so the effect is mild.

benefits.what_it_means: Modest and gradual; improved hydration contributes to a plumper, more elastic-looking surface. Elasticity improvements have been noted in some controlled studies but effect sizes are small.
benefits.mechanism: Sustained hydration of the stratum corneum temporarily improves the mechanical flexibility of skin. Some studies suggest copper peptides in SSF may support structural proteins, though evidence in human cosmetic use is limited.

watchouts.what_to_do: Individuals with diagnosed mollusc or shellfish allergies should patch-test before full-face use; discontinue on any reaction.
SSF is generally well-tolerated but sensitization is possible as with any biological extract. Patch test is prudent for reactive skin types.

watchouts.issue: Mild AHA activity from glycolic acid
watchouts.what_to_do: At cosmetic SSF concentrations the glycolic acid effect is minor, but those using high-strength retinoids or peels in the same routine should monitor for cumulative sensitivity.

consider_separating: high-strength AHAs / BHAs (cumulative exfoliation with SSF's glycolic acid fraction)
retinoids on same application in very sensitive skin
notes: Works well as a hydrating base layer under actives — its humectant matrix can enhance absorption of subsequent serums.
Expect hydration and texture improvements at 4–8 weeks; meaningful elasticity shift (if any) takes longer.
AM or PM use is fine; no photosensitization risk at cosmetic SSF concentrations.
K-beauty context: SSF is a cornerstone of the 'glass skin' layering routine — consistent use of hydrating layers is the mechanism, not a one-ingredient effect.

evidence.summary: Peer-reviewed mechanism data is solid (humectant via glycosaminoglycans/HA; soothing via allantoin; mild exfoliation via glycolic acid — all chemically confirmed in SSF). Human clinical evidence exists but is limited: the most rigorous study is a single-center double-blind RCT (n=50) showing TEWL, elasticity, and firmness improvements vs. vehicle; a 2023 systematic review of 10 clinical trials (n=287 total) found consistent hydration/comfort improvements. Wound-healing data is primarily from animal models. Evidence grade B is appropriate: mechanistic understanding is strong; human RCT data is positive but small-N, single-center, and limited in duration.
